title: Almond-Hazelnut Dacquoise with Coffee Buttercream
summary: Three crisp layers of toasted almond and hazelnut meringue stacked with a silky coffee buttercream.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large egg whites (about 130 g), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: heat the oven to 120 °C (100 °C fan). Draw a 33 x 27 cm rectangle on baking paper, turn it over onto the lightly greased tray.

steps.title: Nuts
steps.text: whizz the hazelnuts, almonds, cornflour and salt in the processor until finely ground, about 20 s, then pulse in the 100 g sugar for the nuts.

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: in the clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the lemon juice on medium until foamy, then on medium-high to soft, billowy peaks. Keep whisking while you add the other 100 g sugar slowly, then whisk 2-3 min more until stiff and glossy. Fold in the nut mix in 2 lots.

steps.title: Spread and bake
steps.text: spread the meringue evenly to fill the rectangle using the offset spatula, then mist the top lightly with water if you have a spray bottle. Bake 1 h 30 min, then turn off the oven and leave it inside, door shut, for another 1 h 30 min. Cooling in the closed oven dries the meringue slowly so it stays crisp and does not crack.

steps.title: Custard base
steps.text: warm the milk until just simmering. Whisk the yolks, sugar, cornflour and salt smooth in the bowl, then pour in half the hot milk, whisking. Tip back into the pan and whisk over medium heat until it bubbles and thickens like warm pudding, 3-5 min; it will pass 85 °C. Cover the surface and chill at least 2 h, then let it come back to room temperature.

steps.title: Buttercream
steps.text: dissolve the espresso powder in the hot water and let it cool. Beat the butter for 3-4 min until pale and creamy. Beat in the custard base in 3 lots, then the coffee and vanilla, and beat 5 min more until light. If it looks curdled, keep beating; it comes together as it warms slightly.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: turn the meringue over, peel off the paper and turn it right side up. With the serrated knife and a gentle sawing action, trim it to 30 x 24 cm, then cut 3 strips, each 24 x 10 cm.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: spread half the buttercream evenly over one strip, right to the edges, and lay the second strip on top. Spread with the rest of the buttercream and top with the third strip, smooth side up. Press gently to level and tidy the sides with the spatula.

steps.title: Chill and slice
steps.text: chill uncovered for at least 3 h to firm. Trim the ends, then slice with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between cuts.

tips: A common mistake is cold custard base; it must be at room temperature, or the butter will split.
Bake the meringue a day ahead and keep it in an airtight box.
Toast the nuts until just golden, as burnt nuts make the meringue bitter.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; the meringue softens slowly. Take it out 20 min before serving.
